original_question: Given a graph G known to be a segment visibility graph, construct a set of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane whose segment visibility graph is G.
target_in_paper: Section 3.1, Open Problem 14: "Given a segment visibility graph G, draw the segments S in the plane whose visibility graph is G."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the reconstruction problem for segment visibility graphs, keeps the scope to graphs already known to be realizable, and asks for a realization by pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane whose visibility graph is exactly the given graph.
missing_details: In this paper, a segment visibility graph is specifically an endpoint visibility graph: the vertices of G correspond to the endpoints of the segments, not to the segments themselves.
The visibility relation for two distinct endpoints is: the straight segment joining them must not intersect any segment of the realizing set S.
The paper's definition explicitly forbids the line of sight from passing through another endpoint or grazing along a segment.
The two endpoints of each original segment are also joined by an edge of G as part of the definition.

To make the question fully stand-alone, one should say that the task is to output some finite set S of pairwise disjoint line segments whose segment visibility graph is exactly G; uniqueness is not required.
A paper-faithful version should not add extra requirements absent from Open Problem 14, such as adjacency-matrix input, integer coordinates, polynomial bit complexity, or a polynomial-time algorithm.
The nearby context distinguishes this reconstruction problem from the separate recognition and characterization problems, so the refined question should stay narrowly on reconstruction only.
refined_question: Let G be a graph that is known to be the segment visibility graph (equivalently, segment endpoint visibility graph) of some finite set S of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane. Here the vertices of G correspond bijectively to the endpoints of the segments in S; two distinct vertices are adjacent exactly when the straight segment joining the corresponding endpoints does not intersect any segment of S, with the additional convention that this line of sight may neither pass through another endpoint nor graze along a segment; and, for each segment of S, the two vertices corresponding to its endpoints are also adjacent. Construct such a set S of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane whose segment visibility graph is exactly G.
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper's intended formulation and is best matched by Section 3.1, Open Problem 14, not by a broader neighboring problem. The only substantive implicit content missing from the draft is the paper's precise meaning of "segment visibility graph," which is defined in Section 1 on the endpoints of disjoint segments, with explicit conventions about forbidden endpoint-passing and grazing, and with each original segment contributing the edge joining its own endpoints. Section 3.1 also separates reconstruction from the distinct recognition and characterization problems, so the refined question should remain narrowly a realization problem. Section 3.2 further confirms why this exact formulation matters: later Hamiltonian-cycle questions become difficult precisely because one may be given only G and not an embedded realization.
